Namespace: [Ankus](/api/ankus/)

Assembly: `Ankus.Runtime.dll`

Changes PostgreSQL configuration settings for the duration of a callback.

```csharp
public static class PgSettings
```

PostgreSQL applies the values as it does a function's <code>SET</code> clause: at a new nest level, with the current
user's privileges, and restored when the callback returns or throws. When a PostgreSQL error aborts the enclosing
transaction or subtransaction, that rollback restores them instead. A plain <code>SET</code> inside the callback outlasts
it, as it does inside such a function.

### Run&lt;TResult&gt;(IEnumerable&lt;KeyValuePair&lt;string, string&gt;&gt;, Func&lt;TResult&gt;)

Runs synchronous work with several settings changed and returns its result.

```csharp
public static TResult Run<TResult>(IEnumerable<KeyValuePair<string, string>> settings, Func<TResult> action)
```

Type parameters:

`TResult`

The callback result type.

Parameters:

`settings` — [IEnumerable&lt;KeyValuePair&lt;string, string&gt;&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.collections.generic.ienumerable-1)

The setting names and values, applied in order.

`action` — [Func&lt;TResult&gt;](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/api/system.func-1)

The work to run on the active backend thread.

Returns: <code>TResult</code>

The callback's result.

PostgreSQL checks every name, value and privilege before the callback runs. A rejected one throws
[PgException](/api/ankus.pgexception/), such as SQLSTATE <code>42704</code> for an unknown setting or <code>22023</code> for an invalid
value, and leaves the transaction usable. Where PostgreSQL cannot start a subtransaction, such as in a
transaction callback, a rejection requires rollback like any other error there. Values use the text form of
<code>SET</code>, including units such as <code>100ms</code>. Do not perform transaction control or asynchronous work in the
callback.
